data.why: The app's real data pipeline downloads and checksum-verifies NIST SRD 46 from an external NIST server, which the sandbox cannot reach, so a schema-valid demo canonical SQLite database is built locally at install time instead.

goals: Find every reported stability constant (log K) for a given metal ion across all available ligands
Filter records by ligand class, reaction stoichiometry (1:1, 1:2, hydrolysis, protonation), temperature, and ionic strength to match a target experimental condition
Compare two complexation records side by side to see which measurement conditions explain a difference in reported value
Spot-check candidate literature references behind a ligand-metal pair before citing a constant
Export a filtered subset of records as CSV for downstream analysis
Identify duplicate or near-duplicate records retained across data sources for provenance

review.summary: The tree describes the explorer's purpose exactly. Its four phases match the README's search → record → compare → references → export flow, and most labels and cited screens hold up. Before filing it, rework the t1 and t9 branch structures, re-test the Ni²⁺ 'bug' (probably two per-source entries for the same ion, which is by design), and add a comparison that differs in measurement conditions.
